thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager: P2 - continuous-batcher backlog growth & node restarts in us-west-2. Affected: /v1/generate routes. Thresholds breached: 95th latency > 3s, OOMs on 3 workers. Link: https://ops.redwood/example/incident/2887654321

leo: seeing consistent KV cache growth on batcher pods -> memory pressure then CUDA_OOM in repeated cycles. Logs attached below.

sara: thanks. are customers impacted or just internal healthchecks?

leo: customer-facing. 2 customers reported elevated latencies, some 429s when retry thresholds hit. Traffic shape: big prefix requests causing long-lived KV entries.

anya: triage: is continuous batching enabled with prefetch/kv_cache on those pods? If yes, we should flip the feature flag and drain.

mike: confirmed continuous_batching=true and prefetch_kv=true in the rollout config for canary group-3. That group got an autoscaler bump last night.

ops-runbook-bot: runbooks matched: "batcher-kv-growth" and "cuda-oom-on-persistent-batching". Recommended immediate mitigations: 1) disable continuous batching on canary, 2) scale down new nodes, 3) force soft-restart batcher service.

leo: trying disable now on one node to validate. (curl to admin)

leo: ```
# disable continuous batching on node group-3
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/feature_flags -d '{"group":"group-3","continuous_batching":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

sara: nice. after disable, let's drain that node and watch the queue lengths. I'll coordinate node drain with infra. @infra-bot can you start draining pods on nodes tagged rg-canary-3?

infra-bot: acknowledged. Starting drain on nodes: rg-canary-3a, rg-canary-3b. Command: `kubectl drain node/rg-canary-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

mike: note: draining will requeue requests to other batchers; if those are already high we might push them over. We should also temporarily bump the per-request latency budget and enable fallback to sync-mode.

anya: propose immediate throttle: set max_batch_size=64 -> 32 and max_concurrent_batches=10 -> 6 for canary. This reduces batching growth.

leo: applying throttle now via rollout config.

leo: ```
# throttle patch
PATCH /internal/config/batcher/group-3
{
  "max_batch_size": 32,
  "max_concurrent_batches": 6
}
```

incident-bot: Update: Flags toggled and throttle patch applied at 2887654372. Monitoring for 2 min.

sara: visual check on dashboard: queue lengths dropped ~40% on canary, memory usage trending down on rg-canary-3a after drain. CUDA OOMs stopped on drained node but two others continuing to log occasional OOMs.

mike: rolling restart of batcher pods on remaining stressed nodes to clear stuck KV caches. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher -n runtime --selector=group=group-3`

leo: restart started at 2887654421. One pod failed to come back: CrashLoopBackOff with error in logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating buffer for kv_cache` then container restarts.

anya: run `nvidia-smi` on that host? Could be driver-level fragmentation.

infra-bot: ran `nvidia-smi`, GPU memory free shows ~200MiB free; some orphaned processes not tied to k8s. Clearing via `pkill -f batcher_orphan` on host rg-canary-3c.

infra-bot: performed cleanup, recreated container, pod now Running.

leo: good. metrics show p95 dropping back to baseline after restarts and throttle; still watching.

sara: customer update drafted: "We've identified a batching regression that increased memory and latency for a subset of nodes. We've disabled the new batching prefetch on canary, applied throttles, and restarted affected workers. We're monitoring and will provide a full postmortem." Send after we see stable metrics for 30min.

mike: we should also revert the canary config change that introduced aggressive prefetch. Who owns that PR? I think @leo.

leo: yeah that was my PR: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/merge_requests/5213. Reverting now.

leo: ```
# revert canary batching prefetch commit
git revert --no-edit 9f2d6b3 --author="leo <leo@redwood.com>"
CI pipeline triggered: https://ci.redwood/repo/5213/pipeline/789
```

ops-runbook-bot: recommended follow-ups: 1) add eviction for long-lived KV entries, 2) add guardrail that disables prefetch when free GPU memory < 1Gi, 3) add alert threshold on batcher queue length growth (10%/5m).

anya: agree. I'll open issues and assign.

sara: any remaining customer impact? latest: two customers saw transient 429s; both have resumed normal behavior. No new complaints in last 10m.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Triggered at 2887654321, mitigations applied by 2887654440. Estimated P2 duration 9m (initial detection to mitigations).

mike: action items captured. I'll follow up on changelog and backfill a canary test that simulates long prefix KV growth.

sara: thanks all. handing off to follow-up owners for post-incident. If anything regresses ping this thread. :thumbsup:
